We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied 29646 to target, got three possible precursors (three branches). Need to select one that can be further processed with next template 1914389, then 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391.

We attempted applying 1914389 to first product (with silyl protecting group). It matched and gave two products: one is "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and second "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". The result tuple includes both? Actually apply_template returned a tuple of two tuples: first product and second product? It seems two possible outcomes. The first is a silyl-protected intermediate with a carbonyl (CC=O). The second is a different molecule maybe from alternative site.

We need to continue with template 1914390 on the product from previous step. Which product matches? We checked both but both returned False for matching 1914390. So maybe need to choose a different branch from 29646.

The other two products from 29646: second product "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" (no silyl on acid? Actually O[Si] attached to acid). Third product "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO". Both have silyl on OH maybe.

We need to find a path where each template applies sequentially. Could also consider that template 1914389 may apply to other product (maybe second or third). We tested second product and got False. Third also not tested. Let's test third product with 1914389.
